one_line_contribution: A paired, pre-registered decomposition claiming that in agentic experience memory the benefit of injected retrieved experience saturates after roughly one item while the cost scales with injected token count largely independent of relevance, plus a per-instance token-budget-matched re-examination (C8a/C8b) that reattributes the reported gains of two published curation methods to the fact that curation shortens the injected text.
closest_prior_work: Two, and the proposal engages only one. (1) The one it names: Distractor-Aware Truncation (arXiv:2608.03297) already builds the length-vs-content disentangling machinery with paired comparisons; the proposal's rebuttal — that its injected content is procedural and non-answer-bearing, so there is no signal-loss term — is real but weaker than claimed, since retrieved trajectories still carry task-format and tool-call-schema signal that behaves like answer-bearing evidence. (2) The one it never cites and should: the in-context-learning demonstration literature, specifically Min et al. 2022 'Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations' (the content of demonstrations, including gold labels, contributes far less than the presence and format of the slot) together with the long line of demonstration-count saturation results and many-shot ICL scaling studies. Injected experience is a demonstration slot. Predictions 1 (decoys reproduce most of the harm) and 3 (content value saturates at one item) are the agentic-memory port of an eight-year-old ICL result, and a reviewer who knows that literature will read the decomposition block as confirmation rather than discovery. What survives that reading is only the curation re-examination table (C7a/C8a, C7b/C8b, C9) — which is exactly the half the proposal itself says is most at risk from reimplementation failure.
strongest_objection: The headline claims are stated at magnitudes the study cannot measure, and the one environment carrying them nearly guarantees the result. On power: the proposal pre-registers an MDE of ~4 percentage points at n=600 with 72-108 discordant pairs. Under that same assumption the paired 95% CI half-width on a net swing is roughly 3 points. Prediction 5 asserts BudgetFirst lands 'within 2 points' of the best curation method — an equivalence margin strictly inside the CI half-width, so it is not estimable at n=600 no matter what the data show. Prediction 2 asserts a content-value offset '<3 points', which the design cannot separate from 0 or from 5. Prediction 4's TOST at ±4 is only marginally attainable and only if the observed delta is almost exactly zero. Equivalence testing needs more power than the corresponding superiority test, not less, and the whole payload of this paper is equivalence claims. On the environment: E1 is tool-augmented multi-hop QA over HotpotQA-distractor + MuSiQue, where the procedural content of every stored trajectory is close to identical ('search the bridge entity, then search the relation'). In a bank that homogeneous, 'content value saturates after one item' is near-tautological — the second through seventh items are literally near-duplicates of the first — and C2(7) same-environment decoys are procedurally indistinguishable from correct retrieval, so prediction 1 is close to guaranteed by construction rather than by the load mechanism. ALFWorld, the one environment where procedural experience genuinely varies per task and where the claim is contestable, is explicitly under-powered at n=200 (MDE 7-8 points) and declared directional only. Third, compounding both: the pre-registered fidelity gate runs on a 100-instance dev split where the MDE is ~10 points, so it will admit or exclude C7a/C7b essentially on noise; if it excludes one, the 'published curation gains are budget artifacts' claim rests on a single reimplemented method, and if it excludes both the paper has no contribution left. Fourth, minor but nameable: the mixed-effects regression's three regressors (relevant tokens, decoy tokens, item count) are near-collinear across the grid — in the C1(k) series items and relevant tokens move together by construction — so the central claim that the relevant- and decoy-token coefficients are indistinguishable is identified almost entirely off two design cells, C4 and C5.
what_would_fix_it: (a) Buy power for the equivalence claims: raise E1 to ~1500-2000 paired instances on the eight decisive conditions, dropping the second decoding seed to a subset (the noise floor does not need full n), and restate every equivalence margin at a level the design can actually reach — or delete 'within 2 points' and 'offset <3 points' and replace them with reported CIs. (b) Add the symmetric matching direction, which is the cleaner test and is currently absent: pad the curation output UP with neutral boilerplate to C1(7)'s token count rather than only truncating raw down to curation's length. If C7a's advantage survives padding-up, it is content; if it evaporates, it is length. This also disarms the objection that C8a is not 'raw retrieval at matched budget' but mutilated mid-trajectory text, and that C8a's per-instance budget is an adaptive-k baseline that could only be computed by first running the curation method it is meant to beat. (c) Move the primary environment to one with genuine procedural heterogeneity (ALFWorld or a web/tool agent) and demote multi-hop QA to replication, or at minimum report a measured per-item procedural-diversity statistic for the bank so saturation is not confounded with a homogeneous bank. (d) Run the fidelity gate on a properly powered split rather than 100 dev instances. (e) Cite and position against Min et al. 2022 and the demonstration-count saturation literature, and state what the agentic-memory setting adds beyond them. (f) Report whether released code exists for A-MEM and MemHarness; a reimplementation-only re-examination of two methods is a thin evidential base for a subfield-level correction.
missing_baseline: A content-free filler arm: neutral task-generic boilerplate injected at C1(7)'s token count with zero memory content (i.e. C0 padded to full length). The grid has C4 (one relevant item plus padding), C2u (unrelated-environment memory) and C0 (nothing), but no cell that isolates the pure load slope with no memory content whatsoever. Without it, the regression's load coefficient is not separable from a 'any memory-shaped text at all' intercept, and the load account cannot be distinguished from 'the first item hurts and the rest are free'. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also demand: the reverse-direction budget match (curation padded up to raw's length, per (b) above), and — given the research track explicitly poses the budget as a decision variable — a learned or calibrated per-step budget to compare BudgetFirst's fixed k* against, since the paper asserts that budget is a first-class design variable while only ever testing a constant.
preprint_collision: Better than most: it names specific arXiv IDs, identifies the correct nearest methodological collision (Distractor-Aware Truncation, arXiv:2608.03297), states the exact scoop scenario, and honestly declares its own coverage limit. But it is not sufficient to establish novelty, for three reasons. First, it is self-reported as six queries truncated by a tool call limit in an area the proposal itself says is moving fast — an admittedly non-exhaustive search is a weakness, not a neutral. Second, it searches only for work making its own claim and not for the precedent that makes half its predictions unsurprising: nothing in the check or the Related Work touches the ICL demonstration-count/saturation literature or Min et al.'s 'demonstration content barely matters' result, which is the strongest existing anticipation of predictions 1 and 3. Third, and most damaging by its own logic, the check identifies 'an appendix-level length-matched ablation inside MemHarness or A-MEM' as the thing that would demote the contribution from correction to systematization — and then does not report having read those two papers' ablation sections. That is not a search problem, it is a two-paper reading task the authors were obliged to do before writing this proposal. I also cannot verify the 2026-dated identifiers (2607.28272, 2606.06036, 2605.16045, 2604.20844) from this review context, and two of them are load-bearing reimplementation targets cited without any statement of code availability, which matters given that Risk Factor 1 names reimplementation fidelity as the single largest threat to prediction 4.
